page: Amazon Web Services c6gn.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated physical cores on the ARM64 architecture, utilizing AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processors running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, providing a ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, but it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 75 Gbps.

Benchmark results show a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The multi-core stress-ng CPU performance is strong, ranking in the top 25% with a score of 72,814.16. In contrast, single-core metrics are weaker, with a Geekbench single-core score of 974.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1,519.29, both falling into the lower percentiles. Memory bandwidth remains average, with read-only large block speeds at 167.25 GB/sec and write speeds at 75.13 GB/sec.

This instance is suited for multi-threaded workloads that can leverage its 48 physical cores and high network bandwidth, such as static web serving, multi-threaded decompression, and software compilation. However, single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and text processing show weak performance. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the Graviton-based architecture offers a dense physical core layout without hyperthreading, making it a viable option for scale-out workloads that require high network throughput but do not depend on high single-core clock speeds or local storage.
